idiom_name: static field initialisers / static constructor / [ModuleInitializer] + hosted-service warm-up
implementation_notes: Eager acquisition is the default semantics of .NET type initialisation: static field initialisers and static constructors are guaranteed to run at most once, before the first instance is created or any static member is referenced, so a resource held in a static field is ready for every consumer. Put setup that must precede everything into a static constructor or a [ModuleInitializer], and put warm-up that operators must be able to diagnose into the host's start-up callback (IHostedService.StartAsync) instead; pre-warmed buffers come from ArrayPool<T>.Shared or an ObjectPool<T> policy rather than a hand-rolled free list. Reserve explicit initialisation methods for work that must fail with an actionable message, and never block on async work inside a static constructor.
pitfalls: Without an explicit static constructor the type keeps BeforeFieldInit and the runtime may run the field initialisers later than expected - only 'sometime before the first static field access' is guaranteed.

An exception in a static constructor is wrapped in TypeInitializationException and the type stays uninitialised for the whole application domain, so an eager failure becomes permanent and un-retryable.
Blocking on tasks or taking locks inside a static constructor risks deadlocking against the runtime's initialisation lock; the documented guidance is not to block there.
